- D: Do not build `link backfill`. Record it in the plan as an open user decision with three options:
  reject it in favour of the shipped evolution-edges seeding pass, amend Invariant #2 for a
  metadata-only carve-out, or record a reading that YAML curation was never "rewriting the past".

- Backfill mutates existing entries' YAML, which collides with Invariant #2 ("never rewrite or
    delete"). Constitution §11: a proposal conflicting with a live invariant "is rejected or must
    first amend the invariant - it cannot silently override it".

- The plan was approved 2026-07-05; the Constitution was ratified 2026-07-14. The sign-off predates

- D: Record two candidate fixes ahead of the band in priority: raise the semantic blend weight
  (`semantic_component = cosine * 3.0`, `semantic_cache.py:927`), and re-examine the recency
  multiplier. Neither is applied in this branch - both need their own held-out fit.

The reason is arithmetic: cosine is bounded by 1, so a perfect
  semantic match contributes 3.0 against one tag match's 12.0, and the measured semantic share of
  `match_score` is 21.6%. It cannot reorder anything separated by more than three lexical points.

Separately, chasing a 73-versus-63 discrepancy
  between two of my own harnesses isolated the recency multiplier: it removes 10 of 120 correct
  answers from the top 8. In a store whose purpose is retrieving old decisions, down-weighting age
  deserves an explicit argument, and `lambda_days=0.01` has never been validated against recall.

- D: Record the Codex arm in PREREGISTRATION.md as a dated append with an explicit no-pooling rule,
  add a `--brief` probe override that `collect.py` excludes from every scored table, and fingerprint
  the parent repo before and after each run into `parent_isolated`.

Two independent facts make the arms
  non-comparable: a different tool surface and system prompt, and a materially thinner transcript -
  Codex `--json` emits `mcp_tool_call` items and the final message but no reasoning items, only a
  token count, so faithfulness can only be judged there against observable behaviour.

Amending by
  append rather than edit is the same append-only discipline the product sells.

- D: `graph`, `trail`, `inspector`, `topbar`, `navigation`, `settings`, `workspace-bar` — each named
  after a region that actually exists in `App.tsx`. `diagram-view` (3) stays below the floor.

I had been proposing pane children from memory and getting the grain wrong. Reading the component
  tree fixed two errors at once.

**`navigation` replaces `context`**: what I had proposed as a child was
  a SECTION inside `<aside class="navigation-pane">`, alongside the topics filter and project stats — the
  pane is the right unit, and at 14 it clears the floor where the section's 7 did not.

And **`topbar` and
  `workspace-bar` are panes I never proposed at all**, both clearing the floor, covering the find bar,
  worktree picker, view switcher, graph scope and edge filters

JNL's question - "why can't the adr reference the constitution location directly?" - was the
  right one; my sidecar design added a fourth file family to solve a problem the event ledger
  already solves.

The separate bindings sidecar (my original design) was declined by JNL and was the worse
  shape. Putting bindings in frontmatter was declined - frontmatter is stable identity per the
  contract, and bindings evolve with revisions, which is what the ledger is for.

- D: `AdrEvent.constitution_refs: tuple[ConstitutionRef, ...]` - `{ref, role}` pairs, role
  `governing|supporting`, refs of the form `constitution:v1#slug` resolved at validation time
  against `<!-- constitution-ref: ... -->` anchor markers in `docs/CONSTITUTION.md`.

The schema is ours: an optional field rendered omit-empty leaves every
  pre-existing record byte-identical, so no schema_version bump, no migration, and the codex
  fixtures' sha256 pins hold. Validation refuses malformed refs, unknown roles, duplicates, and -
  the working half - refs that do not resolve to a real anchor

- D: `pair_affinity.py` builds an area-pair table by lift (n>=3, lift>=2.0, leave-one-out) and
  `topic_candidates.py` uses it to surface extra candidates, each labelled `[pair-expanded]` with
  its lift and n. The two measurements forbidding any other use are in the module docstring.

As a GATE the table scored the known-bad
  hop highest of all (lift 11.30) - from n=1, because that very edge was in the data it learned
  from, which is why leave-one-out and the count floor are load-bearing rather than tidy. As a
  RANKER every topic-derived scorer placed JNL's approved picks at chance (mean rank 3.00 of 5).

- D: `render_adr` renders the title through `_yaml_scalar()`, which quotes a value that contains
  `": "` or `" #"`, ends in a colon, opens with a YAML indicator, or carries edge whitespace. The
  five affected files were repaired by re-rendering, with the repair refusing to write if the diff
  touched anything but the title line.

Quoting conditionally rather than always is what keeps every record written
  before this byte-identical, which matters because three ADRs are sha256-pinned by the codex
  fixtures.
